A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReflectionCoder and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D. Material can be matched across the reorganization, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original code-generation benchmark results and ablations, including multilingual, DS-1000, masking, and positional-embedding experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds data-source experiments, autonomous enhancement, mathematical reasoning, additional coding benchmarks, and training-loss analyses.

M1.justification: The code-generation pipeline, KL objectives, and three masking strategies remain intact. Section 4.5 adds a limited adaptation that treats mathematical chain-of-thought as the reflection sequence and distills it into final-answer generation. The expanded loss-masking explanation largely repeats information already present in v1 Appendix C.

E1.justification: V2 adds APPS and LiveCodeBench script-generation tasks, ClassEval class/function evaluation, and BigCodeBench complex coding tasks. Section 4.5 also adds GSM8K and MATH for training and evaluating mathematical reasoning, extending coverage beyond code. The earlier benchmarks and multilingual coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds O1-Preview while retaining the previous comparators. The new Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct experiment compares distillation with the unmodified model and test-time reflection. The additional coding benchmarks reuse the existing Magicoder-S and OpenCodeInterpreter comparator families.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs vary reflection-data generators, compare training-time distillation with test-time reflection, and introduce Llama-3.1 mathematical reasoning controls. Appendix B.3 specifies zero-shot greedy evaluation and a post-2023-09-01 LiveCodeBench selection. Existing training settings largely persist. Table 11 labels StarCoder as 7B rather than v1's 15B, but retains the scores and 15B description in the prose; an actual model change is unresolved.

E4.justification: V2 adds the 'w/o Reflection Sequence' control, distinguishing the contribution of traces from additional final-answer data. It also adds generator-source comparisons, autonomous enhancement experiments, a negative-input code case study, and training-loss diagnostics in Appendix B.7. The earlier component, masking-order, up-sampling, positional-embedding, and token-masking analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point performance estimates without confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-training-run and seed information. The added tables and training-loss curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores are retained, including DS-33B's 82.9/76.8 on HumanEval/HumanEval+ and 84.1/72.0 on MBPP/MBPP+. V2 adds substantial results in Tables 4-6 and 10, the no-sequence ablation, O1-Preview scores, and loss trajectories. For example, Table 6 reports GSM8K accuracy of 9.9 versus 11.1 and MATH accuracy of 9.6 versus 13.6 without versus with ReflectionCoder; these are new within-v2 comparisons.

T1.justification: Equations 1-2 remain unchanged, but the definition accompanying Equation 2 changes t_prs from tokens of a partly masked reflection sequence to a partly masked reflection instruction. This introduces a local definitional inconsistency with the surrounding procedure. No new theorem, proof, or substantial derivation appears.

C1.justification: The introduction reframes the dataset-construction contribution around automatically generated reflection data and annotation savings, and drops the explicit claim of improvement without extra instructions. The central claims about reflection self-distillation, dynamic masking, and improved one-off code generation remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations concerning the value of reflection traces, self-generated data, filtering versus test-time reflection, negative-input handling, and loss spikes during masking transitions. It argues that GPT-4 data is not essential and qualifies the earlier GPT-4 dependency as a broader reliance on capable models, with open-source alternatives. The RoPE restriction and DS-1000 limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds concrete prompts for APPS/LiveCodeBench and ClassEval. The Ethics Statement newly documents upstream sources and access links for the existing instruction corpus. Original code/data access, training hyperparameters, hardware, filtering instructions, and training templates are largely retained; several new experiments receive limited implementation detail.

R1.justification: Related work adds InverseCoder and AutoCoder, explicitly distinguishing training on reflection sequences from AutoCoder's use of interaction to obtain training data. V2 also adds references supporting the new models and benchmarks, while removing CodeT5+ and MAmmoTH citations. The overall research positioning remains centered on improving one-off generation through reflection-based training.

P1.justification: Most shared prose remains recognizable. V2 edits the abstract, contributions, related work, conclusion, and affiliations; separates the two distillation techniques into methodology subsections; and moves GPT-4 data-construction prompts to Appendix A.1. It also adds Ethics and Acknowledgment sections and simplifies some terminology.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a single-column to a two-column layout. Figure 1 is substantially simplified, tables and prompt boxes are reformatted, and Figure 4's unchanged plots are stacked vertically. V2 also adds four result tables and Figures 5-6 showing the masking schedule and training losses.

improvement.justification: The no-sequence control addresses an important attribution gap: whether gains arise from reflection traces or merely additional answer data. Autonomous Llama self-training directly tests dependence on GPT-4, while broader coding evaluations and mathematical experiments strengthen previously limited generalization evidence. These gains substantially improve the paper despite incomplete details for some additions and the new StarCoder-size and variable-definition inconsistencies.
